Hi Evan / Lina —

Thanks again for the productive conversation this morning. Quick synthesis from our side so everyone has a single view before we dive into a technical work session later this week. If anything below is off, flag it and we’ll adjust.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency spikes during morning peak (08:00–10:00 PT) are causing slow triage and increasing SLA breaches for support workflows.
- Cost volatility when traffic bursts hit — high token generation costs on current managed provider.
- Concern about cold-starts and multi-region failover for redundancy.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 required + VPC peering and audit log retention (13 months).

Primary goals
- P95 generation latency under 200ms for short support prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target of ~250 inference requests/sec during peak (avg prompt 80 tokens).
- Pilot that demonstrates consistent p95 and cost improvements before procurement decision.

Quick technical notes we captured (actionables follow)
- Preferred model family: candidate 7B or 13B open models; willing to test 4-bit quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- KV / prefix caching for repeated support templates will be important to reduce per-request work.
- Multi-region route with primary in us-west and failover to us-east; data residency US-only.

Attachments: brightmeridian_slo_matrix.xlsx (first-pass SLO mapping)

Proposed next steps
1) Karthik and team to send a short technical plan (topology + sizing + pilot metrics) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Schedule a 90-minute deep-dive lab session with your infra folks (suggest Wed/Thu this week; two time windows below).
3) Exchange minimal dataset/sample prompts and peak traces so we can size batching and KV cache behavior.

Proposed slots (PST): Wed 08/18 09:00–10:30 or Thu 08/19 13:00–14:30 — are either good?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendars once you confirm a slot.

Thanks Tessa — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Workload: primarily customer support triage + short answer generation. Typical prompt length 40–120 tokens, average 80.
- Peak pattern: daily spike 08:00–10:30 PT, occasional secondary spike around 14:00 PT. Peak concurrency ~250 rps for ~30–45 minutes, sustained 90–120 rps outside peak.
- Cold start tolerance: up to 300ms for occasional scale-ups, but we want to avoid repeated cold starts during the morning spike.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II in place; we require VPC peering for Private deployment and ability to push audit logs to our Splunk instance.
- Procurement timeline: pilot decision within 6 weeks; final procurement depends on pilot results + legal review.

I’ve attached a short traffic extract and prompt examples (sent separately via S3 link). For the deep-dive session, Wed 08/18 09:00 PST works best for our infra and SRE team.

Subject: Technical plan: pilot topology, SLO mapping, and sizing (summary)

Evan —

Appreciate the additional detail. Below is a concise technical plan we propose for the pilot and the reasoning behind the topology and sizing. I’ll bring a short topology sketch and a cost estimate to the deep-dive (attached).

Pilot goals and success metrics
- P95 generation latency < 200ms for <=128-token requests 90% of the time during peak.
- Sustained peak throughput support of 250 rps with headroom for short bursts to 350 rps.
- Demonstrable 30–40% cost reduction per 1k tokens vs current managed baseline via batching + quantized model variants + cache.

Proposed pilot topology (sketch attached: bm_topology_sketch.pdf)
- Dedicated inference pool in us-west (primary) with autoscaling GPU pool and burst buffer to us-east.
- Smart routing rules: traffic steering by region + fallback to cheaper quantized variant if primary capacity constrained.
- KV cache layer per-instance for common prefixes; prefix caching to avoid repeated decoding for templated prompts.
- Warm pool strategy: maintain a small warm reserve (N=4 GPUs) during morning peak to reduce cold starts.

Model plan and quantization
- 7B float baseline and 13B quantized (4-bit) variant for tradeoff testing. Suggest comparative runs for 48 hours to measure latency/cost.
- Compile-level kernel selection: short-context optimized kernels for <=128 token requests; ensure continuous-batching paths enabled.

Batching and throughput notes
- Target effective batch size 8–16 during peak (based on your prompt-length distribution).
- With batching and KV cache, estimated req/sec per A100x2 node: ~120–160 rps for 7B quantized; estimate 2–3 nodes sustained for 250 rps peak with autoscale headroom. See attached bm_cost_estimate.csv for a rough cost model.

Instrumentation and metrics to collect during pilot
- p50/p95/p99 latency (generation & end-to-end), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cold-start counts, cache hit rate, tail latency by model variant, error rate.
- We’ll provision tracing hooks and token-level cost reports in the Redwood Console for the pilot.

Security and operations
- We can run Private (VPC peering) pilot so audit logs feed to your Splunk forwarder; we’ll share SOC 2 evidence and onboarding checklist pre-session.

Attachments: bm_topology_sketch.pdf, bm_cost_estimate.csv

Next immediate asks
1) Share an S3 link with 24–48h sample traces and a few representative prompts.
2) Confirm Wed 08/18 09:00 PST for the work session and please add your SRE Slack channel so we can share live metrics.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for the 2-week POC and a checklist of test queries to validate SLOs.

—
